name: Belgium — Belgian parties
intro: compare it with Belgian political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Belgium: those represented in the parliament (Kamer / Chambre) and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the parliament (Kamer / Chambre) after the 2024 election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 150 members.

PVDA-PTB.name: PVDA-PTB
PVDA-PTB.priorities: Cost of living, Taxing wealth, Public services, Workers' rights and wages
PVDA-PTB.description: Marxist Workers' Party, the only party organised across Flanders, Brussels and Wallonia; it campaigns for a millionaires' tax and lower energy prices.

Groen.name: Groen
Groen.priorities: Climate action, Affordable housing, Public services
Groen.description: Flemish green party, focused on climate policy, clean air and public transport.

Ecolo.name: Ecolo
Ecolo.priorities: Climate action, Public services, Civil liberties
Ecolo.description: French-speaking green party, which lost heavily in 2024 after years in regional and federal governments.

PS.name: Parti Socialiste
PS.priorities: Public services, Workers' rights and wages, Pensions and the elderly, Public healthcare
PS.description: French-speaking Socialist Party, long dominant in Wallonia, defending wage indexation, pensions and public services.

Vooruit.name: Vooruit
Vooruit.priorities: Public healthcare, Workers' rights and wages, Security and law and order, Reducing immigration
Vooruit.description: Flemish social democrats, in the federal government since 2025, combining social protection with a firmer line on migration and integration.

Volt.name: Volt Belgium
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

Les Engagés.name: Les Engagés
Les Engagés.priorities: Public healthcare, Education, Small business and entrepreneurs
Les Engagés.description: Centrist French-speaking party, successor to the Christian-democratic cdH, which surged in 2024 and joined the federal and Walloon governments.

CD&V.name: Christen-Democratisch en Vlaams
CD&V.priorities: Traditional family values, Small business and entrepreneurs, Security and law and order
CD&V.description: Flemish Christian democrats, historically Belgium's leading party, now a mid-sized partner in the federal and Flemish governments.

Open VLD.name: Open Vlaamse Liberalen en Democraten
Open VLD.priorities: Fiscal discipline, Lower taxes, Civil liberties
Open VLD.description: Flemish liberals of former prime minister Alexander De Croo, heavily defeated in 2024.

MR.name: Mouvement Réformateur
MR.priorities: Lower taxes, Fiscal discipline, Security and law and order, Nuclear energy
MR.description: French-speaking liberals, the largest party in Wallonia since 2024, pushing lower taxes, labour-market reform and nuclear energy.

N-VA.name: Nieuw-Vlaamse Alliantie
N-VA.priorities: More autonomy for Flanders, Fiscal discipline, Reducing immigration, Security and law and order
N-VA.description: Flemish nationalist party and the largest in Belgium; its leader Bart De Wever became prime minister in 2025 and it seeks a confederal Belgium.

VB.name: Vlaams Belang
VB.priorities: More autonomy for Flanders, Reducing immigration, Security and law and order, National identity
VB.description: Far-right Flemish nationalist party seeking Flemish independence and a halt to immigration; the other parties keep it out of government through a 'cordon sanitaire'.
